rules.rule: dated more than a season away from the file it sits in (TML's 2024 Challenger file holds Noumea matches of 2007-2008), or undated: dropped
dated before December 2009: dropped
round label missing or unknown: dropped (it cannot be ordered)
a player's name missing: dropped
TML row dated apart from its event's main draw (qualifying dated the day before or after it; matches of 2026 and Davis Cup rubbers dated by the day played): given the main draw's first date
walkover (no point played): kept, never evaluated
score says BYE for a two-player match: treated as a walkover
walkover marker after games were played: treated as a retirement
retirement: kept, the player who advanced won, flagged
default (disqualification): status other, not evaluated
abandoned or unfinished: status other, not evaluated
score blank or unreadable: status other, not evaluated
completed, but the score is written from the loser's side (read the other way it is a complete win for the recorded winner): read reversed
completed, but the last set is unfinished and the winner short of the sets needed (6-2 0-0): a retirement without its marker, treated as retired
completed, every set finished, the winner ahead but short of best-of (a best-of-3 rubber in a best-of-5 tie): kept, flagged
completed, but the score fits neither player finishing the match: score-derived counts dropped
box score blank for both players: missing
box score all zero for a player: missing, not zero
box score for one player only: missing for the match (return rates need both)
box score with some counts blank (other than service games): missing
service games blank, the other eight counts present: kept, service-game rates missing
service games recorded as 0 with serve points played: service games treated as missing
box score check: negative box-score count; box score dropped
box score check: first serves in exceed serve points; box score dropped
box score check: first-serve points won exceed first serves in; box score dropped
box score check: second-serve points won exceed second serves; box score dropped
box score check: break points saved exceed break points faced; box score dropped
box score check: service games disagree with the games in the score by more than one, whether tiebreaks count as service games or not; service games dropped, the other counts kept
box score check (added): double faults exceed second serves; box score dropped
box score check (added): aces exceed serve points won; box score dropped
box score check (added): breaks conceded exceed service games (checked where service games pass B5); box score dropped
box score check (added): fewer than 4.5 serve points per game in the score (a game has at least 4 points): the counts cover part of the match; box score dropped
played in short sets (first to 4 games; the Next Gen ATP Finals): flagged
a match tiebreak replaces the deciding set (the Laver Cup, some Davis Cup ties, some women's ITF events of 2019): flagged
a 10-8, 11-9 or longer deciding score read as a match tiebreak by its main-tour event's rule (the event's other deciders are certainly match tiebreaks; 13 Oct 2026): counted as one, not as a set
minutes blank or zero: missing
player id blank in the source: the id the same name has elsewhere (else a name-based id)
TML player without a Sackmann id (newer than Sackmann's files): ATP website code kept as the id
both players resolve to the same id: dropped
Sackmann: the same match listed twice in one event (same round and players, same winner); one kept, preferring the row with a box score
TML: the same match listed twice in one event (same round and players, same winner); one kept, preferring the row with a box score
Sackmann: the same event, round and players listed twice with different winners; both dropped
TML: the same event, round and players listed twice with different winners; both dropped
Sackmann: the same match (same round, players, week and score) copied into a second event; the copy under the later tournament id dropped
TML: the same match (same round, players, week and score) copied into a second event; the copy under the later tournament id dropped
the same match id twice after the merge (a TML row of a match Sackmann holds that the links missed): the Sackmann row kept
the recorded loser plays the next round of the event and the recorded winner does not: winner and loser exchanged (the player who advanced won)
a TML-only match whose player already has a Sackmann match in the same event and round (a repeat with a misidentified opponent): dropped
serve points leave out double faults (Sackmann's WTA tour events of 23 Feb - 24 Aug 2015): double faults added to serve points, both players (decision 2026-10-08)

a retirement written without its marker, the score short of a finished match (every other source and the tour's own record call it a retirement; since 22 Oct 2026): RET appended to the score, so it reads as retired (decision 2026-10-08)

one edition of an event at the wrong level (Stage 0's level rules match an event by name and code, not by year; the tour's own record gives the level): the edition's level corrected (decision 2026-10-22)
one edition of an event on the wrong surface (WTA Paris 2013-14 filed as carpet; the WTA, tennis-data and Flashscore give hard): the edition's surface corrected (decision 2026-10-22)
box scores exchanged between winner and loser (confirmed by the WTA's own statistics, an official feed or the score): the nine counts exchanged back (decision 2026-10-08)
service-game counts exchanged between winner and loser: exchanged back (decision 2026-10-08)
box score copied from another match (WTA Adelaide 2 2022 from Adelaide 2021; the same pair's other meeting): blanked (decision 2026-10-08)

box score copied from another match (WTA Adelaide 2 2022), or contradicted by the tour's own box and point record of the match where they agree (since 22 Oct 2026): replaced by the tour's own statistics of this match (decision 2026-10-08)
impossible or stale age (Tennis My Life's 2026 WTA ages written without their decimal point; ATP Challengers of 17 Aug 2020 aged at 16 Mar 2020): the age from the birth date (decision 2026-10-08)
second serves booked as first serves (Roland Garros 2022-2025, Paris Olympics 2024): first serves in and points won on each serve from the official record (decision 2026-10-08)

service games the score disproves or leaves blank (Australian Open, Roland Garros): both set from the score's alternation of serve, from the Slam's own record of who served first (decision 2026-10-08)

event dated in another week than it was played (Tennis My Life gave the third Tenerife Challenger of 2024 the first one's name and date; three reviewers confirmed the date the matches were played): the event's true date (decision 2026-10-14)
Sackmann surface blank: taken from the TML rows of the same event
Sackmann's level code does not separate 250 from 500 (ATP) or 500 from 1000 (WTA): the level TML gives the same matches is used
ambiguous Sackmann level code and no TML match in the event: the code's default kept (A, I and W -> 250, P -> 500, PM -> 1000)
TML files a non-Masters event under M (Winston-Salem 2026): 250
no level rule matches: dropped
box score taken from the official Slam feed (decision 2026-10-06; data/studies/data_continuity/slam_box_overrides.csv)
score and minutes taken from the official Slam feed, TML's being cut short (same decision)
